Sub-issue: Didn't receive notice of right to dispute
Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint because Fair Collections & Outsourcing ( FCO ) continues to violate the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). They have not provided the legally required validation of the alleged debt, they have not provided proof of the initial notice, and they continue reporting an unverified debt to the credit bureaus. Their previous CFPB response was incomplete, unsupported, and did not resolve the violations. 



Failure to Provide the Required Initial Written Notice FCO claimed they mailed the initial written notice on XX/XX/year> and emailed a copy on XX/XX/year>. However, they did not provide any proof to support these statements. They offered : No copy of the alleged letter No proof of mailing No address used No postal confirmation No tracking information Under FDCPA 1692g ( a ), a collector must be able to produce this notice upon request. FCO did not. Their unsupported statements do not meet the legal standard required to show compliance. 



Their Email Claim Is Unsupported and Legally Insufficient FCO also claimed they emailed the notice and that it was confirmed open. This statement is problematic for several reasons. 

First, email is not a legally acceptable method of delivering the FDCPA initial notice unless the consumer has explicitly consented to electronic communication, which I did not. Therefore, the emailif it was even sentwould not satisfy 1692g ( a ) requirements.

Second, FCO provided no evidence of the email they claim to have sent. They did not provide : A copy of the email The sender or recipient email address The email header or metadata A timestamp A delivery confirmation A read receipt A screenshot showing it was opened Without proof, their statement is unverifiable and insufficient. The FDCPA requires documented proof of the required notice, not unsupported assertions. Their inability to produce any evidence strongly indicates the notice may have never been emailed or opened.

Even if the email existed, which is not supported by evidence, it still would not fulfill their legal obligations under the FDCPA.

Failure to Validate the Debt In response to my dispute, FCO provided only an itemized list of charges. This does not satisfy the validation requirements under FDCPA 1692g ( b ). Proper validation requires documentation that the debt is legitimate and accurate, including : The lease agreement The final move-out statement A full rent ledger Proof of each charge Move-out inspection notes Photos or evidence of alleged damage Proof that the apartment sent a final bill Proof charges comply with state law None of this was provided. An itemized statement alone is not validation. Because FCO failed to validate the debt, they were legally required to cease all collection activity, including furnishing it to the credit bureaus, yet they continue to report the account. 



Failure to Provide Required Documentation from the Apartment The apartment was required to provide or request a forwarding address, send a final bill, and provide proof of mailing. No such documentation has been provided by FCO or the creditor. Without these documents, the legitimacy of the charges remains unverified.

Continued Reporting of Unverified Information Despite the debt being disputed and unvalidated, FCO continues to furnish the account to the credit bureaus. This violates : FDCPA 1692g ( b ) collection must stop until validation is provided FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) furnishers must investigate and remove unverified information An itemized list does not qualify as verification under federal law.

Pattern of Consumer Complaints Regarding FCO My experience wit
h FCO mirrors a well-documented pattern of consumer complaints found in public records such as the CFPB complaint database and XXXX  listings. Many consumers report similar issues, including : Failure to send or prove the initial notice Failure to validate debts when requested Reporting unverified information to credit bureaus Incomplete dispute investigations Failure to respond to consumers with supporting documentation I am not asserting that FCO has been found legally liable for all allegations made by other consumers, but these publicly reported patterns indicate concerns regarding their compliance practices. My experience aligns closely with these documented issues. 



Requested CFPB Intervention I respectfully request that the CFPB require FCO and the apartment complex to produce the appropriate documentation, including : From FCO : A copy of the initial 1692g ( a ) notice, proof of mailing, proof of any email sent, a full validation package, documentation authorizing collection activity, and documentation supporting their furnishing of the debt. 

From the Apartment Complex : Any forwarding address recorded, a final move-out statement, proof of mailing, the lease agreement, inspection notes, photos, and a full rent ledger. 

If neither party can produce these documents, I request : Immediate deletion of this account from all credit bureaus A stop to all collection activity Written confirmation of compliance

A refund or credit of interest charges assessed during the period in which my account was unknowingly set to minimum-payment autopay 3. An explanation of why Citibank allows minimum-payment autopay to be set or maintained without explicit, repeated consumer acknowledgment of the interest consequences I am also requesting that Citibank review its autopay design and disclosure practices to prevent other consumers from being placed into unintended revolving debt.

Additionally, my business was denied credit, but I did NOT receive an ECOA-compliant adverse action notice, which is required by federal law. Furthermore, because the credit application was for my business, not my personal finances, a personal hard pull should NOT have been performed unless I explicitly authorized it. At no point did US Bank : Present me with a personal credit inquiry authorization form Notify me in writing of a personal hard pull Obtain my signature or electronic consent Provide clear disclosure about the impact on personal credit My business, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, was denied credit, but the bank has refused or failed to : Provide documentation supporting the decision Provide proof of permissible purpose for the inquiry Provide the required adverse action notice Explain whether the decision was based on personal or business credit factors US Banks actions constitute violations of both the FCRA and the ECOA, and I am requesting CFPB investigation and enforcement. 

DESIRED RESOLUTION I request the following : A written adverse action notice explaining why my business credit application was denied ( ECOA requirement ). 

Proof that I authorized a personal hard inquiry OR confirmation that no authorization exists.

Removal of the unauthorized hard inquiry from all credit bureaus.

A full explanation of US Banks business credit underwriting criteria as required by law.

Confirmation of whether my personal credit was improperly used in determining the denial. 

Assurance that US Bank will update internal procedures to comply with FCRA and ECOA requirements.

I am writing to formally dispute the inclusion of the following account on my credit report : Creditor : ProCollect Account Number : XXXX  Status : Unverified Reason for Dispute This account appears on my credit report as Unverified. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681i, I have the right to dispute any information on my credit report that I believe is inaccurate or can not be verified. According to the FCRA, credit reporting agencies must conduct a reasonable investigation and remove any information that can not be verified within 30 days.

Additionally, the FCRA ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ) requires that only accurate and verifiable information be reported. If an account is marked as unverified, it can not legally remain on my credit file. Reporting unverified information is a violation of my consumer rights under the FCRA. 
Furthermore, please be advised that failure by the credit bureaus or the reporting company to promptly remove this unverified account may result in legal action. Under the FCRA, consumers have the right to sue for damages if their rights are violated, including the continued reporting of unverifiable information. I reserve all rights to pursue legal remedies should this account not be deleted as required by law. 
Request for Immediate Removal Because this account is unverified, I am requesting the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to instruct the credit reporting agency to immediately remove this account from my credit report in compliance with the FCRA. Failure to do so is a violation of federal law and my consumer rights. 
Applicable Laws 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( FCRA Section 611 ) : Requires reinvestigation of disputed information and removal of unverifiable accounts within 30 days.

15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) : Mandates maximum possible accuracy of information reported.

I respectfully request the immediate deletion of this unverified account from my credit report. Please provide written confirmation of the results of your investigation and the actions taken. 
Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this complaint against Bank of America , N.A . regarding the unlawful retention of my business funds following the closure of my business checking account. 

1. Facts Bank of America closed my business account and is currently holding a total balance of {$87000.00}, stating that the funds will be withheld for a minimum of six ( 6 ) months.

The funds consist of : Approximately {$40000.00} related to merchant processing activity {$47000.00} from a separate deposited check, unrelated to merchant transactions Bank of America has explicitly stated that even the {$47000.00} deposited check funds will be held for at least six months, despite the account being closed. 
I have not received any check, disbursement, or lawful documentation justifying this prolonged retention of funds. 

2. Why Bank of Americas Conduct Is Improper and Potentially Unlawful A. Unlawful Retention of Cleared Check Deposit Funds ( UCC Article 4 ) Under Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Article 4, once a deposited check has cleared, a bank has a duty to either : Make the funds available, or Return the funds to the customer upon account closure A bank does not have authority to hold cleared check funds for months without a court order, legal seizure, or statutory requirement. 
Bank of America has provided no legal order or documentation authorizing the retention of my {$47000.00} check deposit. 

B. Improper Use of Risk or Merchant Review to Justify Holding Non-Merchant Funds Even if a bank is reviewing merchant activity, it can not lawfully withhold unrelated customer funds. Holding non-merchant funds under the justification of a merchant review constitutes an unfair and abusive practice under : 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( Consumer Financial Protection Act UDAAP ) C. Violation of FDIC Account Closure and Funds Disbursement Standards FDIC supervisory guidance requires that when an account is closed : Remaining funds must be returned promptly Funds may not be held indefinitely without lawful authority A blanket statement that funds will be held for at least six months without providing a legal basis violates these standards.

D. Failure to Provide Written Legal Justification or Adverse Action Notice Bank of America has failed to provide : A written explanation citing the specific law allowing a six-month hold Any adverse action notice Any documentation of a lawful investigation requiring retention of funds This lack of disclosure violates federal consumer protection expectations and constitutes a deceptive and abusive practice. 

3. Harm Caused As a result of Bank of Americas actions : My business is deprived of {$87000.00} in operating funds {$47000.00} of my own deposited money is being held without legal justification The account is closed, yet funds are withheld I am unable to operate my business or meet obligations 4. Requested CFPB Intervention I respectfully request that the CFPB require Bank of America to : Identify the exact federal statute or regulation authorizing the six-month hold Immediately release the {$47000.00} in non-merchant deposited funds Provide written documentation supporting any continued hold on merchant-related funds Disburse all remaining balances without further delay Correct any violations of federal banking and consumer protection laws

Consumer complaint narrative:
Background I am a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX veteran and I have a property tax exemption that means I do not owe property taxes for my primary residence. When I applied for my mortgage in XXXX, my exemption status was part of the loan process and was provided and accepted during underwriting/closing. 

Problem began after servicing transfer In XXXX, my loan servicing was transferred to Lakeview / XXXX XXXX. Immediately after transfer, the servicer began escrowing and charging property taxes that I do not owe, increasing my monthly mortgage payment by $ XXXX per month. This created a severe and immediate affordability issue for my household. 

I promptly notified the servicer and tried to resolve I flagged the error as soon as the improper escrow charges appeared. The servicer then required that I obtain additional confirmation documentation from the county tax collectors office, despite the exemption having been provided as part of the original loan. The tax collectors documentation process commonly takes 69 months. During that time, my servicer continued billing escrowed tax amounts that were not owed, resulting in an unaffordable payment and escalating amounts due. 

Servicer steered me into forbearance Due to the inflated monthly payment, the servicer advised me to enter forbearance, stating that it would help while the documentation was gathered and that the payment would later be corrected/right-sized. As a result, I followed their direction. 

Harm caused after forbearance Coming out of forbearance, the servicer has required outsized monthly payments in excess of {$6000.00} and is proposing loan modification terms that are substantially worse than my existing mortgage. Their modification terms include : Demanding repayment of the full amount owed including escrowed property tax charges I do not owe, plus interest and related fees ; and/or A modified loan term of 40 years at an interest rate approximately 1.6 % higher than my current interest rate. 

These options are not reasonable because the delinquency and accrued balance are tied to the servicers failure to properly recognize my lawful property tax exemption and to stop escrowing taxes I do not owe. 

What I want ( requested resolution ) I am requesting that Lakeview / XXXX XXXX : Immediately correct my escrow account to reflect that I do not owe property taxes and stop escrowing taxes going forward ; Remove/reverse all escrow charges for property taxes that were not owed, including any associated interest, fees, and penalties ; Correct my account history, including any negative credit reporting or delinquency caused by this error ; Provide a clear written explanation and full accounting of how escrow was calculated, what taxes were paid/attempted to be paid, and where funds were applied ; Provide a workable repayment/payment structure that reflects my correct tax status and does not require me to accept objectively worse terms ( e.g., 40-year term and higher interest rate ) to fix a servicer-caused escrow error.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint regarding Kia Finance Americas refusal to correct an unauthorized buyer designation a

rising from a lease-end vehicle purchase, which has resulted in title failure, lien perfection failure, and financial harm to the actual purchaser.

I was the primary lessee on the original vehicle lease ( Lease Account # XXXX ). At lease end, the vehicle was purchased by XXXX XXXX, who obtained financing independently through her credit union and is the sole borrower on the loan. 

I did not : agree to purchase the vehicle, sign a purchase agreement, sign a retail installment contract, sign a buyer odometer disclosure, or sign a title assignment. 

My only executed document at lease end was an odometer disclosure related to lease return, not purchase.

Despite this, Kia Finance America auto-populated my name from the lease records into post-lease purchase documentation, listing me as a buyer without my consent or signature. This incorrect designation has caused the North Carolina DMV to refuse title issuance, which in turn has prevented the lender from perfecting its lien and has resulted in increased interest charges to the purchaser.

Attempts to Resolve I have made repeated attempts over several months to resolve this directly with Kia Finance America. 

On XX/XX/year>, Kia Customer Care contacted me and stated a complaint would be filed on my behalf. I was then transferred to Kia Finance.

During that call : A Kia Finance representative identified as XXXX asserted that because I was the primary account holder, I was therefore the buyer and that no corrective action was possible. 
When asked to identify any purchase document bearing my signature, none was produced. 
I was repeatedly redirected back to Customer Care.

Upon refusal, the call was escalated to a supervisor identified as XXXX, who maintained the same position and declined escalation. 

During this interaction, it was disclosed that no meaningful notes had been entered in the case file documenting prior calls or the substance of the dispute, despite multiple earlier contacts and the existence of Kia Customer Care file numbers XXXX and XXXX. 

Kia Finances position has consistently been that primary account holder status equates to buyer status, despite the absence of any signed purchase agreement. This position ignores basic contract principles and prevents correction of seller-side documentation errors.

Why This Is a Compliance Issue Buyer designation requires affirmative consent and signature.

Lessee or primary account holder status does not confer purchase authority.

Kia Finance can not identify any document bearing my signature agreeing to purchase the vehicle.

The incorrect buyer designation is a seller-side documentation error.

Kia Finance has refused to issue or coordinate corrective documentation.

As a result, the purchaser has suffered financial harm due to title delay and increased interest charges, and Kia Finance has effectively attempted to shift liability to a non-purchasing party.

Resolution Requested I am requesting that Kia Finance America : 1. Issue or coordinate seller-side corrective documentation, such as a corrected Bill of Sale or seller error correction affidavit, confirming that I am not a buyer and that my name was included in error.

2. Provide written confirmation allowing the North Carolina DMV and the lender to complete proper title issuance and lien perfection.

3. Cease asserting buyer status absent a signed purchase agreement.

Additional Information This matter has been repeatedly stonewalled at the customer-service level, and internal escalation has been refused. I am requesting CFPB assistance to compel regulatory-level review and resolution.

Sub-issue: Confusing or misleading advertising about the credit card
Consumer complaint narrative:
1. The Misleading Headline and " Net Impression '' I was presented with a promotional banner upon logging into my account, which featured the headline : " Unlock an extra 30 % cash back on your holiday shopping! ".

In standard financial terminology, " cash back on shopping '' describes a percentage of the transaction amount. Furthermore, the use of the word " extra '' implies an additive bonus. The " net impression '' of this headline is that the cardholder will receive their standard rewards rate plus an additional 30 % on the transaction totals. 


2. The Contradictory Fine Print The terms of the offer were not clearly displayed on the initial login banner. They were only clarified in an email sent on XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXapproximately two weeks after I first saw the banner and began spending. The body text of this email redefines the offer as earning " an extra 30 % cash back on cash back earned ''. 
This shifts the 30 % calculation from the transaction amount ( as stated in the headline ) to the rewards earnings. This changes the offer from a massive additive bonus ( e.g., 1 % + 30 % = 31 % return ) to a negligible multiplicative bonus ( e.g., 1 % x 1.3 = 1.3 % return ). 


3. Materiality and Injury ( Financial Damages ) This deception was material to my decision-making and directly altered my financial behavior in three specific ways : Lost Opportunity Cost : I charged {$700.00} to this card instead of my alternative card which earns a guaranteed 7 % cash back. I forfeited approximately {$40.00} in guaranteed rewards because I relied on BMO 's implied offer of ~31 %. 
Induced Spending : I made {$990.00} in discretionary purchases solely because I believed I was receiving a 31 % discount. I would not have made these purchases otherwise. 
Behavioral Manipulation : The offer required spending " at least {$1500.00} '' and making " at least 10 qualifying purchases ''. My historical average with this card is roughly 7 transactions totaling less than XXXX XXXXXXXX. Because of this deceptive offer, I spent over {$2500.00} this montha 400 % increase over my normal usagespecifically to meet the thresholds advertised. 


4. Timing of Disclosure The promotional banner appeared approximately two weeks prior to the clarifying email received on XX/XX/year>. This created a significant window where I was induced to spend money based solely on the deceptive " net impression '' of the headline, with no access to the contradictory fine print.

Complaint Narrative I am filing a complaint regarding unfair and misleading interest charges caused by Citibanks payment allocation practices on a credit card account with multiple promotional balance transfers, compounded by inconsistent and contradictory customer service communications.

I had two balance transfers on the same Citibank credit card account : - One balance transfer with a 0 % promotional APR, scheduled to expire on XXXX - A second balance transfer with a 0.99 % promotional APR, which remained active after that date When the 0 % promotional APR expired on XXXX, the APR on that balance increased to approximately 24 %. I made an online payment on XXXX with the clear intent to pay off the balance that had just exited the 0 % promotional period in order to avoid ongoing high-interest charges.

Citibanks online payment system did not allow me to choose which balance my payment would be applied to. Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR 0.99 % promotional balance, while leaving the higher-APR balance unpaid. As a result, interest continued to accrue at approximately 24 % on the balance I was actively attempting to eliminate.

This payment allocation defeated my clear and reasonable intent and caused avoidable interest. The payment screen did not clearly disclose that payments could be diverted to a lower-APR promotional balance, nor did it explain how a consumer could prevent post-promotional interest when multiple promotional balances exist.

Customer Service Assurances and Contradictory Written Responses After discovering the issue, I contacted Citibank customer service on three separate occasions. During each call, I was told that the issue would be corrected, that the interest would be adjusted, and that these assurances were documented in the account notes so that any representative could review them.

I specifically asked for confirmation in writing and was repeatedly told that written confirmation was unnecessary because the resolution was documented internally in Citibanks system notes.

Despite these assurances, I later received written letters from Citibank stating the opposite, denying that any correction could be made. These letters directly contradicted the verbal assurances I relied upon. Copies of these letters are attached to this complaint. I am also attaching call log screenshots showing the dates and frequency of my calls to Citibank customer service.

Due to Citibanks failure to resolve this issue and the continued accrual of interest, I ultimately closed the account. After closure, I no longer have online access to view the detailed interest calculations or statements. I have requested copies of my statements from Citibank for the relevant billing periods and will be provided upon receipt.

Contradictory and Misleading Payment Allocation Explanation Please note that even Citibanks written responses contains internally contradictory language regarding how payments are applied.

The letter states that : Each month 's minimum payment due is applied to principal balances in APR order from lowest to highest.

The letter then states : Payment amounts greater than the minimum due are applied to balances with higher APRs before balances with lower rates.

My payment exceeded the minimum due. At the time of payment, one balance carried an APR of approximately 24 %, while the other carried a 0.99 % promotional APR. Under Citibanks own written explanation, my payment should have been applied to the higher-APR balance first.

Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR balance and continued charging high interest, then relied on this same explanation to state it was unable to apply [ my ] payment as requested. This contradiction made it impossible for me to reasonably understand how to avoid post-promotional interest.

Why This Is Unfair and Deceptive - Citibanks payment allocation practices were not clearly disclosed, particularly in a multi-promotion scenario.

- The online payment system did not allow consumers to direct payments to the highest-interest balance - I relied on repeated verbal assurances that the issue would be corrected - Citibanks written responses directly contradicted those assurances- Citibanks own written explanation of payment allocation is internally inconsistent - I incurred avoidable interest despite acting promptly and in good faith Taken together, this constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, especially when combined with inconsistent customer service representations and a lack of transparent disclosure.

'' The combination of missed communication, misinformation, and lost documentation suggests a systemic problem rather than an isolated oversight. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and Newrez LLC/Shellpoint Servicing Violations ( Post-Transfer and During Moratorium ) : Failure to Provide Debt Validation Notice : Following the loan transfer to SLS and initial communication, I was never provided a written validation of debt notice within the required five days, a clear violation of the FDCPA. 
Fraudulent Breach Letter and Forgery : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX generated a fraudulent breach letter associated with an invalid tracking number and an alleged forged signature on the certified mailing receipt. This letter was supposedly sent out during the federal mortgage foreclosure moratorium ( which was active until XX/XX/XXXX ). The servicer 's actions constitute an unlawful acceleration of my loan, as proper written notification was never validly delivered as required by law and the loan agreement, and was prohibited during that timeframe. 
Violation of Foreclosure Moratorium : The issuance of this breach letter and the acceleration occurred during the federal mortgage foreclosure moratorium ( which applied to federally backed loans like mine ), a clear violation of protections. 
Contradictory Reinstatement Quotes and Hidden Fees : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX provided a reinstatement quote in which it was explicitly noted with a " {$0.00} '' entry, indicating that no legal fees, property preservation fees, late fees, or any other charges would be added. However, these exact fees are clearly shown in my payment history. Furthermore, Shellpoint later provided me with a separate, detailed breakdown of property preservation fees dating from XXXX until XXXX. This discrepancy demonstrates deceptive practices and the imposition of unauthorized fees. 
Dual Tracking : I believe I may have also been a victim of dual tracking, a practice prohibited under CFPB Regulation X of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ). Mortgage servicers are generally prohibited from proceeding with foreclosure while a loss mitigation application is pending review. This violation is further underscored by the improper assessment of home preservation charges while I was actively seeking assistance, which suggests the servicer was simultaneously working toward foreclosure and loss mitigation tracks. 
Relevant Federal Law Violations The actions described above violate specific federal laws and regulations, suggesting systemic failures : CARES Act ( Section 4022 ) : The servicer violated the mandate to grant forbearance upon request ( Failure to Grant Forbearance Upon Request ). The issuance of a breach letter during the moratorium violated Section 4022 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( Violation of the Foreclosure Moratorium ). There was also potential Inaccurate Credit Reporting.

Regulation X of RESPA ( 12 CFR Part 1024 ) : The servicer engaged in prohibited Dual Tracking ( 12 CFR 1024.41 ) by accelerating the loan during a time when loss mitigation options should have been explored and by assessing home preservation charges during that period. The inability to contact home preservation specialists is a Failure to Exercise Reasonable Diligence ( 12 CFR 1024.39 ), a duty that includes informing borrowers of COVID-19 options during required live contact. The general handling of my case suggests a Failure to Provide a Timely Response to loss mitigation inquiries.

Violations of the CFPA : The " explicitly inaccurate information, '' " manufactured fraudulent documentation, '' and contradictory reinstatement quotes are examples of the Misrepresentation and Deception that constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice ( UDAAPs ) under the Consumer Financial Protection Act. 
FDCPA : The servicer failed to provide a debt validation notice following the initial communication as required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.

4. I deposit the closeout check ; Citi then snatches it back On XX/XX/year>, I deposit that check at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX into my account ending in XXXX. XXXX XXXX credits my account for {$7800.00}. 
On XX/XX/year>, XXXX XXXX sends me an alert that my {$7800.00} deposit was returned unpaid by the issuing financial institution because of STOP PAYMENT and debits {$7800.00} from my account. 
In a secure chat that same day, XXXX XXXX confirms : The returned item is Citibank check XXXX. XXXX ( same as XXXX ), The amount is {$7800.00}, and Citibank placed the stop payment. 

So Citi closed my account, issued a closeout check for {$7800.00} from my XXXX account, I deposited it, and then Citi put a stop payment on their own check after I relied on it. 

5. Citis third-party funds story does not match the facts In a later XX/XX/year> letter to me and the regulators, Citi now claims that the funds in question were third-party deposits payable to someone else and that they can not disburse any of it to me, not even {$0.00}.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Formal Regulatory Complaint Against Citibank , N.A .

To : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ( OCC ) Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ( FDIC ) From : DAT Date : XX/XX/year> Subject : Follow-Up Regulatory Complaint Improper Re-Closure of Citi Credit Card Account and Changed Balance Treatment After Prior CFPB-Initiated Reinstatement ________________________________________ I. Parties Complainant : DAT, an individual consumer residing in Florida.

Respondent : Citibank , N.A . ( Citi ), a national banking association regulated by the OCC and subject to CFPB jurisdiction.

________________________________________ II. Background and Prior CFPB Complaint This complaint concerns the same Citi credit card account that was the subject of my prior CFPB complaint in XX/XX/year> regarding an abrupt and unjustified closure of my Citi Simplicity account on or about XX/XX/year>. 
Following that earlier CFPB complaint, Citi reopened the account and confirmed that it was in good standing. 
After the account was reopened, I continued making payments and relied on having a functioning account under the original terms. 
There were no new delinquencies or misuse on my part after the account was reinstated. 
The present complaint arises from Citis new decision, in late XX/XX/year>, to close the account again and to change how my existing balance is being treatedafter I contacted Citi solely to report a lost card and secure the account from potential unauthorized use. 
If helpful, this matter should be linked to my prior CFPB case so regulators can view Citis conduct as a pattern, not as isolated events.

________________________________________ III. Summary of Current Complaint This new complaint concerns Citis : 1. Improper and misleading re-closure of my credit card account after a routine lost-card report where I only intended to block the physical card, not terminate the account.

2. Change in the treatment of my existing balance, including a larger or accelerated amount now demanded by the end of XX/XX/year>, without clear explanation or proper notice. 
3. Refusal to reverse or correct the action, despite my request to reinstate the account under the same terms that applied after the XX/XX/year> resolution. 
4. Potential retaliatory conduct, given the prior CFPB complaint and Citis earlier decision to reopen the account and acknowledge that closure as improper or inconsistent with its obligations.

These actions raise serious concerns under : The prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) ; The Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and Regulation B ( 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ) regarding adverse action notices ; The Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) concerning changes in account terms and required disclosures ; and The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) if this new closure is reported in a manner harmful or inaccurate to my credit profile.

________________________________________ IV. Factual Timeline of New Events 1. XXXX 2025 Period After the CFPB complaint in XX/XX/year>, Citi reopened my account. 
Citi representatives indicated that the account was in good standing. 
I continued to make payments and use the account in a responsible manner. 
2. Late XX/XX/year> Lost Card Report In late XX/XX/year> ( approximately the last week of XXXX ), I called Citi to report that my card was lost. 
My clear intent was to block the lost physical card and protect against unauthorized charges, and, if necessary, receive a replacement card. 
At no point did I request or authorize Citi to close the entire account, nor did Citi clearly inform me that my account would be permanently closed as a result of simply reporting the card lost. 
3. Full Account Closure and Changed Balance Treatment Shortly after my lost-card report, I discovered that Citi had closed my entire account, not merely blocked the lost card. 
Citi then communicated that more money is now due by the end of XX/XX/year> than I previously understood to be requiredeffectively changing or accelerating my repayment obligation. 
This was done without clear, advance disclosure that a lost-card security call would trigger account closure or altered payment terms. 
4. Citis Refusal to Correct the Problem I contacted Citi and stated that they needed to reopen the account immediately, given that : o The account had previously been reopened after CFPB intervention ; o I had been in good standing since that time ; and o I only reported a lost card, which should not by itself justify full account closure or altered balance terms. 
Citis response was that there is nothing we can do and that the account will remain closed with the new payment obligation in place. 
I have not received a clear, detailed adverse action notice explaining the basis for this closure and change in terms. 
________________________________________ V. Legal and Regulatory Concerns 1. Unfair and Deceptive Practices ( UDAAP 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) o Treating a standard lost-card report as a pretext for closing the entire account and changing payment obligations is unfair and misleading, particularly where the consumer has acted responsibly and in good faith.

o The combination of : the prior wrongful closure, CFPB-triggered reopening, and this subsequent closure tied to a routine security call creates a pattern that appears arbitrary and punitive rather than risk-based and transparent.

2. Failure to Provide Proper Adverse Action Notice ( ECOA / Regulation B ) o Under 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) and 12 C.F.R. 1002.9, Citi must provide a timely written adverse action notice specifying the reasons for closing the account.

o I have not received a proper, detailed explanation for why a lost-card report resulted in full account closure and altered balance treatment.

3. Potential TILA Violations Change in Terms/ Balance Acceleration o If Citi has accelerated the balance, increased the minimum payment, or otherwise changed the repayment schedule as a result of this closure, TILA may require specific advance disclosures and notices.

o I was never told that requesting a lost card be blocked would trigger such a change.

4. Potential FCRA Violations and Credit Harm o If Citi reports this new closure in a manner that implies derogatory behavior ( e.g., risk, returned payments, or closed by grantor for cause ), this may be inaccurate and unfairly damaging to my credit.

o The closure of this long-standing accountespecially after it was previously reopened at Citis discretionwill almost certainly harm my credit utilization ratio and scores.

5. Pattern and Possible Retaliatory Conduct o Citis reopening of the account after the XX/XX/year> complaint indicates that the earlier closure was inappropriate or mishandled. 
o Closing the account again after a routine lost-card report, and then refusing to reverse it while changing how my balance is treated, gives the appearance of retaliation or at least disparate, inconsistent treatment of a consumer who previously exercised her rights by contacting regulators. 
________________________________________ VI. Harm Citis conduct has caused and will continue to cause significant harm, including : Credit harm from the loss of a revolving line and potential negative reporting. 
Financial strain and confusion due to a larger or accelerated payment demand by the end of XX/XX/year>. 
Loss of access to a critical line of credit that I relied upon for necessary expenses. 
Emotional distress and loss of trust, particularly given the repetition of adverse action on the same account after prior regulatory involvement. 
________________________________________ VII. Requested Relief I respectfully request that the CFPB, OCC, and any other appropriate regulators : 1. Investigate Citis conduct, including : o The decision to close my account after a routine lost-card report ; o Any change, acceleration, or other alteration in the repayment terms for my existing balance ; o Citis handling of my account in light of the prior XX/XX/year> CFPB complaint and subsequent reinstatement. 
2. Require Citi to : o Reopen my account under the same terms and conditions that applied after the XX/XX/year> resolution ; o Treat my existing balance under the original repayment schedule, without improper acceleration or undisclosed changes ; o Provide a proper adverse action notice that fully explains any claimed justification for account closure, in compliance with ECOA/Regulation B. 
3. Ensure accurate credit reporting, including : o Preventing Citi from reporting this closure in a way that inaccurately implies misconduct or default ; o Requiring Citi to correct any derogatory or misleading tradeline entries related to this closure.

4. Review Citis policies and procedures for : o Handling lost/stolen card reports ; o Treating accounts that were previously the subject of CFPB complaints, to ensure consumers are not penalized or deterred from exercising their rights.

________________________________________ VIII. Preservation of Rights This complaint is submitted without waiver of any legal rights or claims I may have against Citibank, N.A., including but not limited to claims under federal and state consumer protection statutes, contract law, and any other applicable laws. I expressly reserve the right to pursue civil litigation or other remedies if a satisfactory resolution is not achieved.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint regarding inaccurate and misleading credit reporting by FAIR COLLECTION in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

FAIR COLLECTION is reporting a derogatory tradeline on my credit report with the status listed as Collection / Charge-Off and a balance of {$9300.00}. The account contains multiple material inaccuracies and incomplete information that can not be reasonably verified. 

Most notably, the tradeline lists a Reported date of XX/XX/year>, which is a future date. Credit reporting information must be accurate and current. A future reporting date is factually impossible and renders the tradeline inaccurate under FCRA 607 ( b ) and 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ). 

Additionally, FAIR COLLECTION is reporting the account as both a collection and a charge-off. A charge-off may only be reported by the original creditor. FAIR COLLECTION is a third-party collection agency and has not demonstrated that it is the original creditor or otherwise authorized to report a charge-off status. This dual status is misleading and materially inaccurate. 

The tradeline is also incomplete, with required fields such as last payment date, monthly payment, loan type, and loan term left blank. Reporting materially incomplete information violates FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 2 ) and makes the account unverifiable as reported. 

I previously disputed this account, and the credit bureau responded with a generic statement that the account meets FCRA requirements. However, no explanation was provided as to how a future reporting date or improper charge-off designation could be verified. A boilerplate response does not satisfy the requirement for a reasonable reinvestigation under FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ). 

Because the information reported is inaccurate, incomplete, and internally inconsistent, it should be deleted or fully corrected. FAIR COLLECTION has failed to meet its obligations under the FCRA.

At the time of these reversals, I did not receive any advance notice. I later learned that USAA had placed letters in the secure inbox inside the USAA app. My app notifications were not enabled, and I was unaware of these messages. Only after USAA had already reversed the provisional credits and created the large negative balance did a USAA representative assist me in turning on app notifications. USAAs own recorded phone calls will confirm that I was not notified prior to the reversal of the provisional credits. 
Improper Use of VA XXXX Benefits On XXXX XXXX XXXX, my VA XXXX Compensation in the amount of {$3800.00} was deposited into my USAA account. Because USAA had previously reversed the provisional credits and driven my account to a large negative balance, USAA immediately absorbed this entire VA XXXX payment into that negative balance. My VA XXXX benefits are federally protected. Under 38 U.S.C. 5301 ( a ), VA benefits are exempt from levy, attachment, seizure, or setoff. USAAs use of my VA XXXX compensation to cover a negative balance created by the reversal of provisional credits appears to violate this protection. 
Regulation E and Investigation Concerns USAA denied my fraud claim and justified its decision by stating that the transactions were outside the depository agreement date. This explanation is vague and does not demonstrate that the disputed transactions were authorized. Under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ), a financial institution must conduct a reasonable, good-faith investigation, provide clear written notice of its findings, and meet strict timing and notice requirements before reversing provisional credits. 

In my case, USAA reversed the provisional credits on XXXX XXXX XXXX, without providing effective prior notice. Placing letters into an in-app inbox that I was not configured to receive notifications for does not meet the spirit of Regulation E notice requirements, particularly where the reversal of those credits would drive my account deeply negative and lead to the seizure of my VA XXXX compensation.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/2025, Wells Fargo provided me with written confirmation that my refinance loan was approved and ready to close. The message explicitly stated, Congratulations! Your loan is ready to close, and included finalized loan terms, payment amounts, and a rate lock expiration date. This represented final underwriting approval ( clear to close ). 

XXXX days later, on XX/XX/2025, I was contacted and told that a secondary level quality assurance review required additional documentation related to my employment and income. I promptly provided all requested documents, including pay stubs and documentation of federally protected FMLA leave. 

Despite having already received final approval and despite my employment and income being accurately disclosed throughout the process, Wells Fargo later withdrew the loan approval. I was informed verbally and by email that the decision was based on a secondary review concluding that my debt-to-income ratio exceeded allowable limits due to the exclusion of overtime income. 

Why this is a problem : This action is deeply concerning for several reasons : Final approval was already issued. 

Wells Fargo represented in writing that my loan was approved and ready to close. Withdrawing approval after clear to close is highly irregular and contrary to reasonable consumer expectations. 

The decision relied on a single paycheck taken out of context. 
Wells Fargo relied heavily on one post-leave paycheck that reflected reduced hours due to personal family priorities following the birth of my second child. A single paycheck does not establish an income trend, especially when two full prior years and year-to-date earnings show strong, consistent income. 

My income reduction was temporary and fully explained. 

I took federally protected FMLA leave in XXXX and XX/XX/2025 and then temporarily reduced hours upon return while relying on savings. I am a registered nurse in a hospital system with constant overtime availability and specialized training that gives me ongoing access to additional income. My earning capacity did not decline. 

The lender performed a post-approval review that overturned underwriting without transparency. 

Wells Fargo has stated this was due to a secondary QA review, but has not clearly explained how or why this review was permitted to override an already issued clear-to-close decision. 

The situation feels misleading and unfair. 

I reasonably relied on Wells Fargos final approval. Withdrawing a mortgage at this stage feels like a shady and deceptive business practice, particularly when the reasons cited were known or knowable before approval was granted. 

Regulatory concerns : I am concerned that Wells Fargo may not have complied with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and Regulation B, which require : -Clear, timely, and specific written notice of adverse action -Consistent and non-misleading underwriting practices -Good-faith treatment of borrowers who reasonably rely on lender representations

b'[CFPB Complaint Draft: Defective AdverseAction Notice and Failure to Provide Required ECOA/FCRA Disclosures]
[Respondent: First National Bank of Omaha (FNBO)  Adverse Action Notice Compliance / Credit Services]
[Reference / FNBO Notice Date: Reference No. XXXX  dated XXXX XXXX XXXXDate mailed to FNBO / Proof of receipt: Mailed via Certified Mail; XXXX  delivery confirmation dated XXXX XXXX XXXX (tracking XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX).
Relief requested: See Requested Relief section below.]
1.) [Summary of complaint]
On XXXX XXXX XXXX FNBO mailed me an adverseaction notice regarding my credit card application (Ref. XXXX). The notice is partially illegible and internally inconsistent, and therefore fails to state the specific principal reasons for the adverse action in a clear, readable manner as required by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B (12 C.F.R. 1002.9). The notice also fails to provide clear, nonmisleading creditscore disclosures and related documentation required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V (15 U.S.C. 1681m; 12 C.F.R. 1022.72). I mailed FNBO a written demand for corrected notices and supporting records; FNBO received that demand on XXXX XXXX XXXX. I ask the CFPB to investigate and require FNBO to provide the relief listed below.

2.)  [Chronology (key dates)]
XXXX FNBO obtained credit score (per FNBO notice).XXXX FNBO mailed adverseaction notice (Ref. XXXX).XXXX I mailed a written demand to FNBO identifying illegibility and requesting corrected notice and records.XXXX XXXX certifiedmail delivery confirmation shows FNBO received my demand.
3. Specific legal deficiencies alleged
A. ECOA / Regulation B (12 C.F.R. 1002.9)

The adverseaction notice must contain a statement of the action taken and either (a) the specific principal reasons for the adverse action or (b) a clear statement of the applicants right to request those reasons. The FNBO notice contains garbled and corrupted text (headings and portions of the reasons section are illegible), preventing a reasonable consumer from identifying the principal reasons for denial. This renders the notice substantively defective and noncompliant with Reg B.

B. FCRA / Regulation V (15 U.S.C. 1681m; 12 C.F.R. 1022.72)

When an adverse action is based in whole or in part on a consumer report or credit score, the user must disclose the credit score, score range, date, provider, and key factors that adversely affected the score. FNBOs notice presents overlapping and ambiguous lists (reasons you did not score well vs. key factors) and fails to clearly tie the score factors to the adverse decision. The presentation is confusing and does not meaningfully explain how the score affected the decision.

C. Consumer Credit Protection Act (FCRA subchapter)

Because FCRA disclosure obligations are part of the Consumer Credit Protection Act framework, FNBOs defective implementation of FCRA disclosures also violates the CCPAs consumerprotection objectives.

D. Record retention and automated decision records

Regulation B and supervisory guidance require creditors to retain application and decision records sufficient to demonstrate compliance. FNBO must preserve and produce automated decision logs, scoring outputs, and model inputs used in my application decision.

4. Harm and why relief is needed
The defective notice deprived me of the ability to understand the principal reasons for denial and to meaningfully exercise my right to obtain a statement of specific reasons or to correct inaccurate information.

The ambiguous score disclosures prevent me from assessing whether the credit decision relied on inaccurate or incomplete information and from disputing errors with the consumer reporting agency or FNBO.

Without the requested records (consumer report copies, scoring output, model name/version, automated decision logs), I cannot verify the accuracy or fairness of FNBOs decision or determine whether systemic problems exist that could harm other consumers.'

Over several years, I have experienced repeated failures with U.S. Banks mobile check deposit system affecting both personal and business accounts. The problem is not isolated or incidentalthe structure and design of the system are fundamentally misleading.

The app walks users through the entire deposit process, accepts front and back images of the check, accepts the entered amount, and explicitly indicates the deposit is completed or done. When a bank confirms a deposit as done, consumers reasonably expect that the deposit has been received and processed. In reality, this confirmation is unreliable and misleading.

This inconsistency demonstrates that even when customers report the issue, it continues to occur. The system relies on undisclosed, manual verification by customers rather than clear confirmation by the bank. The app should clearly state at the time of deposit how customers can confirm successful receipt, or automatically notify them if a deposit fails. 

Consumers reasonably rely on a banks confirmation and often discard checks after a completed deposit. This design creates a serious and ongoing risk of financial loss without notice. This requirement was introduced after the late payment had already been reported and after my refinancing options had become limited.

XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) This same pattern occurred previously. During a prior refinance, I was required to bring approximately {$1000.00} in additional funds to close after similar last-minute requirements were introduced. The refinance was completed, but my monthly payment increased afterward, which was later attributed to escrow changes. 

At the time, I accepted that explanation, but seeing the same sequence of events repeat has raised serious concerns about whether these practices are proper, transparent, or compliant with VA servicing and consumer protection rules. 

Key Concerns Requirements involving a non-borrowing spouse introduced late in the process Late payment reporting coinciding with refinance attempts and limiting borrower choice Unexpected demands for additional funds immediately prior to closing Repeated outcome of higher monthly payments after refinancing Lack of clear, early disclosure of these requirements Apparent pattern, not an isolated incident I am concerned that these actions may constitute unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) and XXXX conflict with VA refinance protections, including restrictions on conditioning or steering borrowers through servicing leverage. 

I am requesting that : The servicer provide a written explanation, with citations, for : Why non-borrowing spouse ID was required Why multiple months of payments were required outside the refinance payoff Confirmation that VA and CFPB rules were followed in both refinance attempts A review of whether the late payment reporting was accurate and properly timed A review of whether I was improperly restricted or steered during refinancing Correction of any inaccurate reporting and appropriate remediation if violations are found

I received a phone call that displayed as Wells Fargo on my caller ID and appeared to originate from a legitimate Wells Fargo phone number. The caller represented themselves as a Wells Fargo fraud prevention employee and provided a detailed scenario claiming my account had been compromised. 

The caller asked verification-style questions ( such as whether I was in XXXX, Georgia ) XXXX which reinforced the legitimacy of the call. Unknown to me at the time, my Wells Fargo account had already been compromised. During this call, unauthorized activity occurred, including internal transfers moving funds from my savings account into my checking account and an unauthorized cash advance taken on my Wells Fargo Visa card and deposited into my checking account. 

The caller then falsely claimed that fraudulent actors were removing funds from my account through XXXX XXXX and instructed me to secure my money by following specific steps. Relying on the Wells Fargo caller ID, the impersonation, and the belief that I was speaking directly with Wells Fargo fraud prevention, I transferred {$18000.00} as instructed.

Immediately after the call ended, I felt uneasy and promptly contacted Wells Fargo directly to report the incident. I filed a police report and followed up with Wells Fargo repeatedly. Despite this, Wells Fargo never requested screenshots, documentation, or a copy of the police report number and contact information of the XXXX XXXX XXXX who took my report, nor did they conduct a detailed interview with me. 

Wells Fargo has now denied my fraud claim, asserting that the transaction was authorized because I initiated the transfer. I dispute this conclusion. My actions were taken under deception, impersonation, and caller-ID spoofing, during an active account takeover. Authorization obtained through fraud and misrepresentation is not true authorization. 

Additionally, the unauthorized Visa cash advance occurred without my consent and should be treated separately under credit card protections. Wells Fargos denial appears to rely on a blanket assumption of customer fault without a reasonable investigation as required under Regulation E and applicable consumer protection laws. 

I am requesting that Wells Fargo conduct a proper investigation, reconsider the denial, and reimburse the funds lost due to impersonation fraud and account takeover.

XXXX ) Why Citibanks handling appears improper under federal law a ) Nature of the dispute : goods not delivered as agreed, wrong delivery location Under CFPBs official interpretation of the billing error resolution rule, disputes about goods or services not delivered as agreed include, among others, delivery to the wrong location.

Investigate possible violations of the FCBA and Regulation Z when creditor communications are unclear, contradictory, or improperly place the burden on the consumer for evidence not required by federal rules. 

Attachments and evidence Photo evidence of deliveries to wrong addresses. 

Chat transcript with Wayfair showing refusal to accept correct evidence, and insistence on police report.

Notices from Citibank regarding dispute outcomes on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/year>. 

Closing remark I acted in good faith to resolve a clear case of nondelivery to my address, provided evidence, followed Citibanks instructions, and was repeatedly told the case would be reopened or that evidence should be provided, yet the resolution denied my dispute. Under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005.2 ( m ) ), an unauthorized electronic fund transfer is XXXX initiated by a person other than the consumer without actual authority, and Regulation E does not require a consumer to prove the identity of the individual who made the transaction only that the consumer did not authorize it. 

Additionally, reliance on device or IP data alone does not constitute proof of authorization, particularly where a minor had access to the device. Minors can not legally consent to financial transactions or gambling activity. 

I believe Wells Fargo failed to properly apply Regulation E standards and prematurely denied my claim without sufficient evidence that the transactions were authorized by me.

Separately, I obtained information from a data broker that my credit information had been sold or supplied as part of their dataset. The data broker identified Citi as a source for information obtained through this recurring account review process.

I question whether this level of frequency is necessary to service an existing account, especially when I have a credit freeze in place and have not sought new credit from Citi.

If Citi is using my information for marketing or resale purposes under the cover of account review, I believe this may go beyond the permissible purpose of account review and may violate the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and/or related privacy and consumer-protection laws. 

Sale or disclosure of my credit information to data brokers : Through a data broker, I learned that my credit informationapparently derived from these recurring Citi pullswas included and sold as part of the brokers dataset. I did not provide any consent to Citi for my detailed credit information to be sold or redistributed in this way. I am concerned that Citi may be monetizing my consumer report information without proper authorization, transparency, or opt-out options.

The furnishing of inaccurate and inconsistent information constitutes a violation of federal law and industry standards. Information that varies between credit bureaus or can not be substantiated with competent evidence must be corrected or deleted and can not lawfully continue to be reported.

3. FCRA 616 & 617 Civil Liability for Willful or Negligent Noncompliance Any failure to delete fraudulent information may result in : Actual damages Statutory damages Attorney fees Punitive damages These violations may be pursued in federal court.

4. FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 6 ) Duties of Furnishers After Notice of Identity Theft Once a furnisher is notified of identity theft, they are prohibited from reporting the account further and must block and delete it.

Continuing to report a fraudulent account after receiving this notice is unlawful.

5. FACTA Section 112 Fraud Alerts & Blocking Duties Upon receiving notice of identity theft, the bureau must : Block the fraudulent accounts Remove them from reports Prevent reinsertion unless certified as accurate Reinsertion without certification is another federal violation.

6. FDCPA Violations ( If Any Accounts Are in Collections ) Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 ), no collector may attempt to collect a debt that : Is fraudulent Can not be validated Was created through identity theft Attempting to collect on an identity-theft account constitutes false representation and unfair practices under 807 and 808.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint because Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax continue to report a XXXX  XXXX bankruptcy public record on my credit file after multiple disputes, even though the record can not be lawfully verified. 

I am disputing that this public record can not be verified at the original source, and under federal law, unverifiable information must be deleted. 

The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which is listed on my credit reports as the court or source of this record, clearly states on its official website that : The Clerks Office does not report bankruptcy information to credit reporting agencies The Court does not verify bankruptcy information for any credit bureau or third-party vendor The Court has no input into what credit reporting agencies publish on consumer reports These statements are publicly posted at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  In addition to the Courts published policy, I obtained written confirmation directly from the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX stated clearly : The XXXX XXXX does not report or verify bankruptcy cases to credit reporting agencies, and it has no input as to what the credit reporting agencies have on record regarding any given bankruptcy case. 

The Court further confirms that it does not furnish data, does not verify data, and does not confirm the accuracy of bankruptcy information used by credit reporting agencies. These statements were provided as part of my disputes.

This means the only original source of a bankruptcy record refuses to verify information for credit reporting purposes. Once that fact is known, no credit bureau can lawfully claim that the record has been verified. 

Despite this, all three credit reporting agencies continue to report the bankruptcy and return disputes as verified.

Because the Court does not furnish or verify data, there is no authorized source that can verify this record.

Each bureau nevertheless claims verification : TransUnion admits in its Public Records Policy that it does not obtain bankruptcy data from courts, and instead relies on third-party vendors such as XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX These vendors are data aggregators and are not furnishers under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2.

Experian states only that the company that reported the information has certified it as accurate, without identifying who that company is or how verification occurred.

Equifax lists the Court as the reporting agency, yet directs consumers to XXXX, which then redirects consumers back to Equifax, creating a circular verification loop with no verifying authority. 

I formally requested the Method of Verification for this unchanged or verified public record, as required by FCRA 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ). No bureau provided : The name and address of the data source used to verify the bankruptcy The documentation relied upon to verify accuracy Any confirmation that verification occurred with an authorized furnisher This information has never been provided, even though the item continues to be reported as verified.

Under FCRA 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ), any item that can not be verified must be deleted. Instead, the bureaus continue publishing unverifiable information while refusing to explain how verification occurred.

This conduct violates multiple provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including : 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to ensure maximum possible accuracy 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) Failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ) Failure to provide the Method of Verification 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ) Duty to delete unverifiable information 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) Reliance on unauthorized furnishers Additionally, because the bankruptcy was filed in Alabama, the continued misrepresentation of the source and verification of this record constitutes deceptive conduct under the Alabama Deceptive Trade Practices Act ( Ala. Code 8-19-5 ), including misrepresenting the nature and source of consumer information and consumer rights. 

I also requested a XXXX consumer disclosure over two months ago, and again more than a month ago, and nothing has been provided, preventing me from even disputing the data allegedly relied upon. 

This ongoing loop of verification without an actual verifying authority has caused repeated harm and frustration and leaves me with no meaningful way to correct my credit file. 
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND PROOF OF IDENTITY ATTACHED

I immediately contacted Synchrony when I received that letter, but I was young and unfamiliar with how to escalate the issue, and my concerns were dismissed. 

I did not understand the severe impact that these delinquencies would have on my credit report until recently. I have since begun making payments with the collection agency. However, these missed payments were not caused by failure or unwillingness to paythey were the direct result of access restrictions and lack of support from both Venmo and Synchrony Bank.

This Venmo account is the only negative item on my credit report, and it exists solely because my Venmo account was frozen and I was given no method to update my payment information or access my billing statements. 

I am requesting that the CFPB review this situation and require Synchrony Bank to remove the inaccurate delinquencies from my credit reports, as they do not accurately reflect my payment behavior and were caused by circumstances outside of my control.
